title: What to prune, what to preserve
subtitle: Data pruning · Elastic models · Post-training blogs · Chinchilla close reading
intro: Two focal papers study pruning training examples and model units; technical blogs add synthetic-data and post-training details. Papers dated October 14–15 are overlap-window additions, not today’s releases. The Chinchilla classic derives optimal allocation conditional on a credible empirical loss surface.

articles.paper: Hard Way, The Only Way: Provable Merits of Training on Hardest Examples
articles.authors: Elvis Dohmatob
articles.title: 2N: not simply the hardest examples
articles.dateNote: First posted 2026-10-15 00:00 EDT · v1 · Overlap-window addition
articles.evidence: Read §§2, 4–5 and Appendix E; focus on squared loss

blocks.text: Sorscher et al. (2022) studied pruning-induced changes to learning curves. [3] Here the setting is Gaussian linear classification: dimension \(N\), sample count \(P\), perfectly aligned generator/test/pruner directions, and ridgeless squared loss. [1]

blocks.tex: \phi=\frac NP,\quad T=|G|,\ G\sim\mathcal N(0,1),\quad p=\Pr(T\in A),\quad \mu_k=\mathbb E[T^k\mid T\in A],\quad\nu=\operatorname{Var}(T\mid T\in A)
blocks.label: Proportional high-dimensional limit, then small phi; A selects margins

blocks.text: The paper reduces classification error to an angle; retention must exceed the dimension/sample ratio. [1]
A conditional-density bound yields a variance bound; optimization over retention gives the key chain from Appendix E: [1]

blocks.label: The bound minimizes at p=2phi; a thin band asymptotically attains it, retaining about 2N samples

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The optimal set is a near-boundary thin band excluding the origin, not \([0,c]\). A perfect pruner is not free, and this is not an LLM theorem. General convex-loss analysis uses replicas. We focus on the solvable case; inconsistent bandwidth notation in the manuscript is avoided by using the density bound. [1]

articles.paper: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
articles.authors: Walter Simoncini · Dheeraj Varghese · Gertjan J. Burghouts · Cees G. M. Snoek
articles.title: Freeze weights, learn one cross-budget ranking
articles.dateNote: First posted 2026-10-14 13:58 EDT · v1 · Overlap-window addition
articles.evidence: Read the method, Table 3 and appendix calibration protocol

blocks.text: Fixed-target pruning typically repeats work for each budget. Here only global MLP-neuron/head scores \(z\) are learned; backbone \(\theta\) stays frozen. Let \(b\) denote removed FLOPs and \(\kappa_b\) the cost-weighted ranking threshold. [2]

blocks.label: Compact method rewrite; sg stops threshold gradients; hard masks at deployment

blocks.text: Fourteen targets (5%–70%), 300 Adam calibration steps; ViT-B uses batch 32 and 2,000 unique images by default. One ranking yields nested subnetworks, not optimization-free adaptation. [2]

blocks.caption: Table 3: AugReg ViT-B/16, ImageNet-1k top-1 k-NN accuracy (%). [2]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Evidence mainly supports vision/bidirectional encoders, not autoregressive language generation. Calibration cost and inference FLOPs are distinct budget axes. [2]

articles.paper: Scaling Indic Pretraining: 2.8 Trillion Tokens and an Open Data Generation Pipeline
articles.authors: AI4Bharat · NVIDIA
articles.title: Indic: corpus inventory is not training budget
articles.dateNote: 2026-10-16 · Technical blog; blog date is not model release date
articles.evidence: Read the cited technical sections; not independently reproduced

blocks.text: Translate, judge, repair, transliterate: 75/100 is a rubric threshold, not accuracy. The 2.8T-token inventory includes shared-source language/script variants and already includes 438.4B recovered tokens. Nemotron CPT uses 10B Indic tokens, natural plus synthetic, so stage gains do not isolate synthetic data. This adds the data side to yesterday’s Nemotron coverage; the corpus is still marked forthcoming. [4]

articles.paper: Welcome Beam: a 501B open model you can own, customize, and scale
articles.authors: Ben Burtenshaw · Merve Noyan · Pedro Cuenca
articles.title: Beam: language adherence, not reasoning accuracy
articles.dateNote: 2026-10-16 · Technical blog; blog date is not model release date
articles.evidence: Read the cited technical sections; not independently reproduced

blocks.text: One epoch of Multilingual-Thinking LoRA SFT changes requested-language adherence from 3/16 to 16/16 held-out prompts: tiny sample, no reasoning-correctness evaluation. Separately, the GRPO recipe uses 32 prompts × 8 responses, group advantages and truncated importance sampling, without KL/entropy penalties. A runnable recipe is not demonstrated downstream improvement. [5]

articles.title: Muse Spark: attention-only LoRA on 816B
articles.dateNote: 2026-10-15 · Technical blog; blog date is not model release date
articles.evidence: Read the cited technical sections; not independently reproduced

blocks.text: Experts remain frozen; LoRA targets four attention projections. The reported run uses 64 H100s, 500 steps, length 2,048 and packing, taking about two hours. Training token accuracy rises 72%→84% and loss falls 1.26→0.57; these are training metrics, not held-out capability gains. [6]

articles.paper: Apertus 1.5 Release Notes
articles.authors: Hanna Yukhymenko · Oleg Lavrovsky · Y Metz
articles.title: Apertus: post-training can erode long-context ability
articles.dateNote: 2026-10-15 · Technical blog; blog date is not model release date
articles.evidence: Read the cited technical sections; not independently reproduced

blocks.text: Weights were released July 24; this is a new technical write-up. Five stages: SFT → long-context SFT → RL → DPO → SDPO. Reasoning traces are added only where non-thinking fails; tool trajectories require execution verification. Long-context SFT restores ability eroded by short-context SFT; no isolated causal ablation is established here. [7]

articles.paper: When agents self-improve, what should persist?
articles.authors: Val Alexander
articles.title: Self-improvement: protect tests, not just instructions
articles.dateNote: 2026-10-14 · Technical blog; blog date is not model release date
articles.evidence: Read the cited technical sections; not independently reproduced

blocks.text: This technical synthesis proposes separate tests for goals, role, memory and behavior, separating development, acceptance and final audits while keeping evaluators outside candidate mutation scope. LIP-Eval is a proposal without pilot data or calibrated thresholds, not a validated stability guarantee. [8]

articles.dateNote: First posted 2026-10-15 13:58 EDT · v1 · Overlap-window addition
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; theorem and experiment details not checked

blocks.text: Shared experts reduce representation variability while fine-grained segmentation enlarges routing space. Token-adaptive expert suppression shrinks exploration. The abstract reports gains across model scales, not an extrapolatable scaling exponent. [9]

blocks.text: Explicit generative mechanisms produce environments, tasks and rubrics; independent audits check target recoverability. There are 2,135 training tasks from 1,037 worlds. More data and genuinely solvable tasks are distinct; no universal scaling law is claimed. [13]

articles.paper: MetaExp: Learning to Self-Improve through Experience via Verifiable Cross-Task Environment Scaling
articles.authors: Renhao Li · Xinjie Shen · Yang Su · Jianhong Tu · Derek F. Wong · Dayiheng Liu · Min Yang

articles.dateNote: First posted 2026-10-15 04:29 EDT · v1 · Overlap-window addition

blocks.text: Across 1,000 task families/4,956 trajectories, fixed tools or latent workflows coexist with changing tasks to train experience transfer; downstream weights stay frozen. Domain-excluded tests support transfer, not unlimited self-improvement or a power law in environment count. [14]

articles.paper: The Density of Thought: Predicting and Steering Reasoning in Large Language Models
articles.authors: Tanush Kalhan · Anupam Chattopadhyay · Sriram Ranga · Amritendu Mukherjee

articles.dateNote: First posted 2026-10-15 01:31 EDT · v1 · Overlap-window addition
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; theorem and experiment details not checked

blocks.text: Six model scales, two training paradigms, only 60 GSM8K problems: the density-variance/correctness relation weakens with scale and reverses after RL distillation. Direct steering changes accuracy 60.0%→8.3%; a small-sample negative result, not a universal law. [15]

articles.authors: Yunhao Ni · Yuxin Guo · Jie Luo · Wenjun Wu · Lei Huang

articles.dateNote: First posted 2026-10-15 04:21 EDT · v1 · Overlap-window addition

blocks.text: For arbitrary-depth standard spline-KANs, the abstract states a worst-case exponential-in-dimension coefficient lower bound on isotropic Sobolev balls. classic.title: Chinchilla: from an empirical surface to optimal allocation
classic.authors: Jordan Hoffmann · Sebastian Borgeaud · Arthur Mensch et al.
classic.dateNote: Historical classic: first posted/read v1, 2022-03-29; NeurIPS 2022
classic.evidence: Read §§1–3.4, 4.1 and Tables 2–3; visually checked the PDF tables
classic.question: Discussion: with deployment budget \(C_{\rm total}=6ND+\kappa NQ\), where \(Q\) is lifetime generated tokens, how does optimal model size vary with Q? What measurements identify kappa without conflating hardware throughput and FLOPs?

blocks.text: Kaplan et al. (2020) favored larger models and less data under fixed compute. [32] Chinchilla re-estimates allocation with over 400 runs: the goal is not convergence, but maximal loss reduction per finite FLOPs budget. [30,31]
Let \(N\) be parameters, \(D\) training tokens and \(C\) training FLOPs. This is an empirical model with positive coefficients, not a neural-network theorem. [30]

blocks.label: Original parametric fit; E is the irreducible term

blocks.text: Substitution of the budget constraint balances marginal gains, not the two loss terms themselves:

blocks.tex: \frac{\partial}{\partial\log N}\left[A N^{-\alpha}+B\left(\frac C{6N}\right)^{-\beta}\right]=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\alpha A N^{-\alpha}=\beta B D^{-\beta}
blocks.label: Algebra conditional on the empirical model

blocks.caption: Original Table 2: N* proportional to C^a and D* to C^b. The three estimates are close, not identical. [30]

blocks.label: Our direct consequence: a constant token/parameter ratio additionally requires alpha=beta

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: “About 20 tokens per parameter” is not universal. Schedule length must match training duration; intermediate points on a long schedule are not optimized short runs. Data mixture, repetition and inference cost can change applicability. [30]
